mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month preceding the prediction is associated with tightened financial conditions that reduce near-term equity discounting, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the prior month
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during tightening episodes (t-test p > 0.05); or FEDFUNDS remains above 4.0% for ≥3 consecutive months without SPX loss.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL is negative (deflationary surprise), investors anticipate lower future inflation, prompting a shift from real to nominal discounting that depresses S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in deflationary months (t-test p > 0.05); or inflation surprise index (IC) > -0.2 over the same horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in PAYEMS (labor market strength) accompanied by a decline in UNRATE (labor supply) creates a labor-market tightness signal that, when persistent for ≥2 months, is associated with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥3% month-over-month while UNRATE falls by ≥0.2% over two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive in such labor-market tightness episodes (t-test p > 0.05); or the interaction index (Rank IC) < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in GDPC1 (goods orders) exceeding 5% suggests weakening business demand, which reduces future earnings expectations and produces negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change < -5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative in such episodes (t-test p > 0.05); or GDPC1 recovers within one month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in INDPRO (industrial production) accompanied by a sustained rise in RSAFS (retail sales) indicates sector-specific supply-demand misalignment that depresses confidence and yields negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -2% while RSAFS monthly change > 1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in such episodes (t-test p > 0.05); or the interaction index (Rank IC) > 0.10.

mechanism_narrative: During periods when UNRATE falls below 5% for three consecutive months (labor supply loosening), S&P 500 60-day forward returns tend to be positive as investors anticipate wage growth and demand expansion.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE monthly change < -0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive in such regimes (t-test p > 0.05); or UNRATE recovers within two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in HOUST (housing starts) for three consecutive months, while FEDFUNDS remains below 1%, signals a housing soft landing with accommodative policy, producing positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly change < -2% for three consecutive months and FEDFUNDS < 1.0% for the same period
regime_hint: housing market soft landing with policy accommodation
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in such episodes (t-test p > 0.05); or the interaction index (Rank IC) < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE exceeds 7% for two consecutive months (high labor supply), accompanied by a decline in INDPRO of ≥1%, it signals weak demand absorption in a large labor pool, leading to negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE monthly change > 0.5% and INDPRO monthly change < -1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in such episodes (t-test p > 0.05); or the interaction index (Rank IC) > 0.10.
